title: Conditional probability and Bayes' rule
summary: Conditional probability and Bayes' rule by hand on small numbers: a medical test and a spam filter, natural frequencies, the law of total probability, odds form (prior odds times likelihood ratio), and updating on two pieces of evidence.
written: Written by Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5) on 17 Nov 2026, for the audience in docs/seed-context.md (small steps, hints, terms defined first). Every example was chosen so each hand computation is an integer or a simple fraction; every answer key is re-derived with sympy by tools/validate_courses.py.

sources.name: Bayes' theorem (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Opened 17 Nov 2026. The statement P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B), the odds form O(A|B) = O(A) x P(B|A)/P(B|not A) (posterior odds = prior odds x Bayes factor), and the drug-test example where a positive from a 99% test on a rare group is often a false positive.

sources.name: Pishro-Nik, Introduction to Probability, Statistics, and Random Processes, section 1.4 (probabilitycourse.com)
sources.note: Opened 17 Nov 2026. The definition P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B) as shrinking the sample space to B. Bayes' rule and total probability on the same book's following pages were not opened; those parts rest on the Wikipedia article and on sympy.

sources.name: Seeing Theory, Bayesian Inference (Brown University)
sources.note: Opened 17 Nov 2026. A medical-test example computing P(disease | positive) from prevalence and test accuracy; used for the framing of lesson 1.
